title.narrative: Access to Improved WASH facilities and Socio-Agro Economic Livelihoods Promotion in six villages

description.narrative:
The background of the project aims to contribute to CAFOD’s Food and Livelihoods Security and the Emergency Preparedness, Response and Recovery thematic programme frameworks – as set out in the CAFOD Sierra Leone and Liberia Country Strategy Paper (2016-2021). The project will be implemented in communities that were severely affected by the Ebola outbreak and are in the rebuilding their lives. The Ebola outbreak affected every household in the John Thorpe community claiming 1000 lives and affecting household income. Furthermore, the community is among one the most underserved in the western area districts with little and in some instances poor access to portable water, electricity, road and other essentially services. Several children were made orphans as a result of the Ebola outbreak which ravaged the community; homes where boarded up while children orphaned children were sent to interim care centres and to other extended family members. Many families lost their income especially those that where left behind with the burden of caring for orphaned children. Markets and other income generating activities such as fishing, sand mining were halted due to the nature and spread of the disease. The outcomes of this project therefore is seeking to rebuild the lives of Ebola victims as well as contributing to the Sierra Leonean Presidents’ Recovery Priorities, which is a 24 month plan that includes Water and Agriculture as key sectors in reinstating Ebola victim lives.
Caritas Freetown is an organisation that has a track record of working in the selected communities providing livelihood support and a mobile clinic facility. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the relevant lines ministries- Water resources/ Ministry of Health MoHs, to provide communities with access to safe drinking water where there is the need and a hygienic environment. In order to support the communities with livelihood and income generating opportunities through the Ministry of Agriculture and food security the project will provide small farmers access to improved seeds with technical trainings and supervision that will increase agriculture production.
